events.title: Not Just a Kid: An Exploration of Childhood in the United States Through Puppets
events.description: The ALab in the Department of Anthropology invites you to the opening reception of the exhibition by Angela Clark, “Not Just a Kid: An Exploration of Childhood in the United States Through Puppets” on October 9 (Friday), 12:30pm at Schleman 300. Lunch will be served at the opening. The exhibit will be open on weekdays from noon-2PM, until October 23rd. About the exhibit: The hegemonic thought about childhood in the United States is that children are not whole persons as they are yet to become the idealized form of adult. Hegemonic notions of time dictate that children are yet to be considered “worthy” as they are expected to mold themselves into their culture’s expectations, while not yet being seen as a valid community member. This exhibit critiques the damaging notion that children are simply “human becomings” by exploring their unique relationship to hierarchical paradigms. Children are often overlooked in conversations about systemic injustice, so working within The ALab’s mission to decolonize research, this exhibit utilizes puppets as an approachable and flexible artform to explore childhood through a decolonial lens. Artist Bio: Angela Clark (she/her), is a third year Purdue undergraduate student. She is an intern with The ALab, studying Anthropology and Development and Family Science, and currently exploring Western colonial attitudes towards childhood, childism, and children as a marginalized group in the United States. She is a puppet maker and uses puppets as a medium for multimodal research. Her puppets have been shown in community theater productions as well as educational spaces as a tool of artistic and academic expression. If you are interested in showing the exhibit to your students outside the above-mentioned open hours, please feel free to email Angela Clark at clar1026@purdue.edu to arrange a visit.

events.title: 2026 SUPPLY CHAIN CONSULTING LECTURE SERIES
events.description: PURDUE STUDENTS ARE INVITED Students across Purdue majors and programs are warmly invited to attend any or all sessions. Join us to learn directly from industry professionals, ask questions, explore career paths, and connect classroom ideas with real-world supply chain and consulting practice. ABOUT THE SERIES The 2026 Supply Chain Consulting Lecture Series connects Purdue students with experienced supply chain executives, consultants, alumni, and industry professionals to explore how organizations solve complex supply chain and operations challenges in practice. The series is an integral part of SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting, a 3-credit experiential learning course that transforms the classroom into a professional consulting environment. Student teams apply supply chain theory, data analytics, AI-enabled tools, and structured consulting methods to real-world business and industry challenges. THE THREE-PILLAR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING MODEL Consulting & Industry Study Projects — Students learn by solving real business and industry problems through corporate-sponsored consulting engagements and advisor-guided industry studies.Mentoring Program — Experienced alumni and industry professionals coach student teams on problem solving, analytics, project management, executive storytelling, and professional development. Jeffrey R. Powers, retired IBM executive and Purdue alumnus, chairs the Industry Advisory Board.Industry Lecture Series — Practitioners bring current challenges, emerging technologies, leadership lessons, and real-world decision making directly into the classroom. SCOM 469 builds on Purdue’s university–industry partnerships and experiential projects with organizations including Wabash, Rolls-Royce, Corteva, Taste, and other corporate and industry partners. For Fall 2026, students will work through two experiential project pathways: the corporate project Taste Omnichannel Dining Service Optimization and the industry study Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply-Chain Resilience. WHY ATTEND? Learn from experienced professionals — See how practitioners approach ambiguous, high-impact supply chain problems.Understand professional practice — Explore consulting, leadership, sourcing, planning, program management, and digital transformation in action.Connect analytics and AI to execution — See how data, analytics, and AI shape consulting strategy and day-to-day supply chain decisions.Connect classroom frameworks to real decisions — Examine constraints, cross-functional trade-offs, and the realities of implementation.Build your professional network — Meet Purdue alumni and experienced industry professionals while exploring supply chain career paths.All Purdue students are welcome. You do not need to be enrolled in SCOM 469 to participate. Attend the sessions that match your interests, come prepared to ask questions and share perspectives, and use the series as an opportunity to learn and build professional connections. FALL 2026 LECTURE SCHEDULE SEPTEMBER 3 — Consulting 101 Isaac Tipton — CEO, Prowire USA The opening session introduces the foundations of consulting and structured problem solving. Drawing on professional experience, the speakers will discuss how consultants approach ambiguous business problems, work with clients and teams, communicate insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. SEPTEMBER 17 — Program Management in Supply Chain: From Plan to Execution Michelle Kozlowski — Senior Program Manager, Amazon Catherine “Cathy” Nash — Sales & Operations Execution Planner, Constellation Brands Strong strategies create value only when organizations can execute them. This session focuses on program management, planning, coordination, accountability, and execution—examining how supply chain professionals move from plans and priorities to operational results across people, processes, and functions. OCTOBER 1 — Trade-Off Management + Cross-Functional Procurement & Sourcing Decisions Amanda Tronchin — Finance & Strategy Consultant, Pinnacle Strategy Group Eduardo Da Silva-Witzke — Aftermarket Sourcing Analyst, Cummins Inc. Supply chain and procurement decisions frequently require balancing competing objectives across cost, service, risk, quality, capacity, and strategic priorities. This session explores how professionals structure trade-offs, collaborate across functions, and translate financial, operational, and strategic considerations into sourcing and procurement decisions. OCTOBER 15 — Leadership, Influence & the Human Side of Supply Chain Consulting Kriti Gupta — Director of Operations, Amazon Nilo Cedeno-Guadamud — Global Category Manager, Wabash Analytics alone rarely produces organizational change. This session explores the human side of supply chain leadership and consulting—including stakeholder influence, relationship building, communication, team leadership, negotiation, and the ability to move organizations from insight to action. OCTOBER 29 — AI in Supply Chain: From Consulting Strategy to Everyday Execution Vishal Madisetti — Associate, Emerging Platforms, KPMG US Brookelle Mathieson — Life Sciences Supply Chain Management Consultant, Accenture Possible contributor: Khushi Karmokar — Procurement Analyst, ThoughtSpot AI is changing both how consultants solve problems and how supply chain professionals perform everyday work. This session explores practical applications of AI, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies—from consulting strategy and transformation initiatives to operational decision support, procurement, and day-to-day execution. NOVEMBER 12 — Planning, Constraints & Supply Chain Systems Thinking Kyle Harshbarger — Supply Chain Engineer, Marathon Petroleum Lauren Heiss — Senior Technology Consultant, EY The final session brings together planning, constraints, technology, and systems thinking. The speakers will connect MRP/ERP concepts, bottlenecks, lessons from The Goal, and real-world planning challenges to the broader question of how supply chains operate as interconnected systems. The session will also explore supply chain career paths and how the strategic role of the supply chain function varies across industries. CONNECTING INDUSTRY AND THE CLASSROOM The Industry Lecture Series is not designed as a collection of stand-alone guest presentations. Each session is integrated with students’ consulting and industry-study work. Student teams are encouraged to bring questions from their projects into the classroom, apply lessons from speakers to their analyses, and reflect on how different professionals approach similar challenges across industries. Student ambassadors will also work directly with speakers before selected sessions to help prepare and contextualize the lectures, providing another opportunity to develop professional communication, stakeholder-management, and networking skills. He was the emergency preparedness advisor to the Louisiana Recovery Authority in the aftermath of hurricanes Katrina and Rita and led the California Healthcare Surge Planning which was the first of its kind in the U.S. in terms of scale and scope. events.title: Bang On A Can All-Stars: 90/90
events.description: 90/90 celebrates the music of composers Philip Glass and Steve Reich and their 90th birthday milestones. The Bang on a Can All-Stars have collaborated with and performed the music of fellow New Yorkers Philip Glass and Steve Reich for more than 30 years. Now, as a tribute to these living legends—and their upcoming 90th birthdays—the All-Stars are presenting landmark works by the pair on tour. Released by Philip Glass in 1982, Glassworks is among his most successful and most-loved albums, but Glass has never performed the complete work live with his touring ensemble. In this concert, the All-Stars will perform a brand-new arrangement of Glassworks in its entirety, alongside Reich’s acclaimed rock quintet 2×5 and New York Counterpoint, in honor of these two legendary composers and their birthday milestones.

events.title: Executive Forum with Jeff Swartz, Chief Executive Officer for Seaman Corporation
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Jeff Swartz is Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors of Seaman Corporation, a global manufacturer headquartered in Wooster, Ohio. Since joining the company in 2020, he has led its strategic direction and global operations, focusing on sustainable growth, innovation, and long-term value creation. Prior to Seaman Corporation, Jeff served as President of Moen North America, a $1.5 billion business, and previously held senior leadership positions in global operations, supply chain, and retail. Earlier in his career, he spent 23 years with Armstrong World Industries, serving in a variety of manufacturing, sales, operations, and general management roles in both the United States and internationally. Jeff has lived and worked in China, England, Germany, Switzerland, and the United States, bringing extensive global leadership experience and a broad perspective on business strategy, operations, and organizational development. In addition to his responsibilities at Seaman Corporation, Jeff serves on the Board of Directors of LATICRETE International, Inc., a leading global, family-owned manufacturer of construction solutions. Jeff holds a B.S. in Industrial Engineering from The Pennsylvania State University and an MBA from Columbia Business School.
